_note: Feature definitions for /features/* pages. Slug matches categories.json feature_categories array. Each feature gets a programmatic page comparing tools that have it.

scheduling.name: Scheduling
scheduling.definition: Calendar-based assignment of jobs to specific technicians at specific times.
scheduling.description: Scheduling is the base of field service software. At minimum it shows a calendar (day, week, month) where the office assigns jobs to technicians. Fuller implementations add drag-and-drop reassignment, availability that accounts for existing jobs and drive time, color-coding by job type or status, recurring jobs for maintenance contracts, and mobile sync so technicians see schedule changes as they happen. A tool that has a calendar is not necessarily one that can run a full dispatch board, so test it with a real day's jobs.
scheduling.why_matters: Without proper scheduling, trades businesses lose money in three ways: double-bookings (two technicians sent to one job, or one technician booked for two jobs at once), idle gaps (technicians with open time the office cannot see), and missed appointments (a job request that does not reach the calendar). Each one is a job you paid to win and then lost or delivered late.
scheduling.buying_tips: Test scheduling on three things: speed (how fast can the office reassign a job mid-day?), visibility (do technicians see schedule changes on their phones right away?), and warnings (does it flag conflicts before they happen?). If you run many jobs a day across several technicians, look at dispatch features such as suggested assignments by location and skill, and see the dispatching and AI dispatcher pages.

faqs.q: What's the difference between scheduling and dispatching?
faqs.a: Scheduling assigns a job to a technician in a time slot. Dispatching is the live side: sending that technician, routing between jobs, sending ETAs to customers and reassigning work when the day changes. Field service platforms such as Housecall Pro, Service Fusion and Workiz list both; check how each handles a job that runs long.

faqs.q: Do I need scheduling software if I have a Google Calendar workflow?
faqs.a: A shared calendar can work for one person. Once you have several technicians, customer records, recurring jobs and a need to see changes on the phone, field service software handles those together, where a calendar app does not keep customer and job history. Some tools, such as Jobber, sync with Google Calendar, so you can keep seeing jobs there.

faqs.q: How do recurring jobs (weekly mowing, monthly maintenance) work in scheduling?
faqs.a: Field service platforms that support recurring jobs let you set a customer on a weekly, every-other-week or monthly cadence and create the future visits. The difference is in rescheduling: when one visit moves, do the later ones move too? Test that with a real recurring customer during the trial.

dispatching.name: Dispatching
dispatching.definition: Real-time assignment and routing of jobs to field technicians, with mobile sync.
dispatching.description: Dispatching is what happens after the schedule is built and the day starts. Good dispatching shows where technicians are (GPS), allows quick reassignment when delays stack up, sends ETA notifications to customers, orders jobs to reduce drive time, and matches each job to a technician with the right skills and equipment. Some platforms add suggested assignments; ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro, for example, uses technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates.
dispatching.why_matters: Drive time is a cost you do not bill for, and it grows with every technician and stop. Good dispatching sends each job to a qualified technician nearby, reshuffles the day when a job runs long, and keeps routes tight. Customers benefit too: ETA notifications and updates when a technician is running late cut down on missed appointments and complaints.
dispatching.buying_tips: Check three things: live location of technicians on a map, customer ETA messages (text or app), and matching jobs to skills and equipment. Some platforms add suggested assignments (ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro is one example). Test dispatch on one of your own busy days, from a desktop and from a phone, before you rely on it.

faqs.q: What is route optimization in dispatching?
faqs.a: Route optimization orders the day's jobs across technicians to reduce total drive time. It matters for businesses with many stops per day on set routes, such as pest control, lawn care and pool service. Test it on one of your real days before you rely on it.

faqs.q: How does AI dispatcher differ from regular dispatching?
faqs.a: AI dispatch tools recommend a technician for each incoming job from several factors; ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro, for example, uses technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates. In regular dispatching a person makes each decision. Either way, the dispatcher should be able to override a suggestion.

faqs.q: Can I dispatch from my phone instead of a desktop?
faqs.a: Some field service apps let you schedule and assign jobs from a phone, but the experience differs between tools. If you dispatch from the truck, run a full day's dispatching from the mobile app during the trial, including moving a job and reassigning it.

invoicing.name: Invoicing
invoicing.definition: Creating, sending, and tracking invoices for completed work, with payment collection.
invoicing.description: Invoicing in field service software covers the path from finished job to payment: creating the invoice from the work order, sending it by email or text with a payment link, taking card and ACH payments, tracking what is overdue, and syncing to accounting (QuickBooks, Xero). Fuller implementations add recurring invoices for service plans, automatic payment reminders, partial payments, deposits and financing for large jobs.
invoicing.why_matters: With manual invoicing, the bill waits until someone in the office types it up, and a mailed invoice then waits for a mailed check. Sending the invoice from the job site with a payment link skips the typing and the mail: the customer gets the bill when the work is done and can pay online.
invoicing.buying_tips: Look for: invoices created from completed work orders without retyping, sending by email and text with a payment link, built-in card processing, partial payments and deposits, recurring invoices for service plans, and a QuickBooks or Xero sync. Check which QuickBooks edition each tool supports and which way the sync runs: Jobber syncs one way to QuickBooks Online only, Housecall Pro syncs with QuickBooks Online and one way to QuickBooks Desktop (QuickBooks sync starts on its Essentials plan), and FieldEdge markets a real-time, two-way QuickBooks integration.

faqs.q: Can I send invoices via SMS instead of email?
faqs.a: Some field service platforms send invoices by text with a payment link. A text suits customers who do not check email often; confirm the feature and any text charges during the trial.

faqs.q: How does in-app payment processing compare to separate Stripe?
faqs.a: Compare each platform's published rates for cards, ACH and instant payouts with a standalone processor's. For reference, Stripe's US pricing page lists 2.9% plus 30 cents per successful domestic card transaction (checked October 2026). Some field service platforms process payments through a connected Stripe account, so ask which processor sits behind the platform.

faqs.q: Can I take deposits before starting a job?
faqs.a: Deposit support differs between tools, so check it if you sell large jobs (replacements, roofs, remodels), where a deposit lowers the risk of a cancellation after you order materials. Test a deposit, the job and the final invoice in one trial run.

estimates_quotes.name: Estimates & Quotes
estimates_quotes.definition: Creating professional quotes with line-item pricing, sending for customer approval, converting to jobs.
estimates_quotes.description: Estimating turns a lead into a booked job. Strong implementations pull line items from a pricebook, attach photos from the visit, capture the customer's e-signature, follow up automatically on quotes that have not been approved, convert an approved quote into a job, and offer good/better/best options. Some platforms add pricebook automation; ServiceTitan's pricebook, for example, can pull supplier price changes through Pricebook Connect.
estimates_quotes.why_matters: The share of quotes that turn into jobs, and the average value of each, drive a trade business's revenue. Software that sends a professional quote from the job site, offers options and follows up on unsold quotes works on both. The more quotes you send, the more those gains add up.
estimates_quotes.buying_tips: Test: how fast a technician can build a typical quote in the field, good/better/best options, e-signature, photo attachments, automatic follow-up on unsold quotes, and pricebook integration. If you sell large jobs, check whether financing can be offered inside the quote and which lenders the platform supports.

faqs.q: What is good/better/best pricing and why does it matter?
faqs.a: Three-tier quoting (for example a basic repair, a mid option with an upgraded part, and a full replacement) lets the customer choose rather than accept or reject a single price, and it shows upgrades the customer might not ask about. Check whether a tool lets the customer pick an option and sign in the same step.

faqs.q: How fast can a tech create a quote in the field?
faqs.a: It depends on the tool and on how well your pricebook is set up: picking items from a pricebook is quicker than typing each line. We have not timed tools, so build the same quote in each one during the trial and compare.

faqs.q: Should quotes integrate with consumer financing?
faqs.a: For large jobs (system replacements, roofs, panel upgrades), financing shown inside the quote lets the customer apply without leaving it. Housecall Pro and Jobber add Wisetack financing to quotes, and ServiceTitan works with GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance. Ask each platform which lenders it supports and whether the application happens inside the quote.

payment_processing.name: Payment Processing
payment_processing.definition: In-app credit card and ACH payment collection, with payouts to your bank account.
payment_processing.description: Built-in payment processing means you do not need a separate Stripe or Square account to take payments in the app. Fuller implementations take cards, ACH and mobile wallets, offer instant payouts for a fee, run recurring billing for service plans, handle partial payments and deposits, and send payment links by text or email. Check each platform's published rates, and ask whether processing is its own or a connected Stripe or Square account.
payment_processing.why_matters: Taking payment at the job site, or sending an invoice by text with a payment link, removes the wait for a mailed invoice and a mailed check. Customers can pay by card or phone when the job is done instead of writing a check later.
payment_processing.buying_tips: Compare fees against a standalone processor: Stripe's US pricing page lists 2.9% plus 30 cents per successful domestic card transaction and 0.8% for ACH Direct Debit, capped at $5 (checked October 2026). Look for ACH support (it can cost less than cards on large invoices), the fee for instant payouts, recurring billing for service plans, partial payments, and who handles card security compliance. Ask whether processing is the platform's own or a connected Stripe or Square account, since that decides who you call when a payment fails.

faqs.q: What are typical FSM payment processing fees?
faqs.a: It depends on the platform, so get the published rate card before you sign. For comparison, Stripe's US pricing page lists 2.9% plus 30 cents per successful domestic card transaction and 0.8% for ACH Direct Debit, capped at $5 (checked October 2026). Ask whether instant payouts cost extra.

faqs.q: Can I take tap-to-pay or Apple Pay payments?
faqs.a: Some platforms support card readers or tap-to-pay on a phone, and some accept Apple Pay or Google Pay through payment links; Skimmer and Paythepoolman, for example, list Apple Pay and Google Pay. Check the options in each platform's payment settings during the trial.

faqs.q: How fast do payments hit my bank?
faqs.a: Payout timing depends on the processor and your account. Ask each platform for its standard payout schedule, and what instant or same-day payouts cost, in writing.

customer_portal.name: Customer Portal
customer_portal.definition: Self-service web interface where customers view jobs, invoices, schedules, and account history.
customer_portal.description: Customer portals let homeowners and business customers manage their own accounts: see upcoming appointments and past invoices, pay balances, update payment methods, view service history, request more work, manage service plans and approve quotes. That takes repeat 'when is my next appointment' and 'what was my last invoice' questions off the office.
customer_portal.why_matters: Every question a customer can answer in a portal is a call or email the office does not have to handle. The more recurring customers each office person handles, the more a portal saves, and easy repeat-service requests help keep those customers.
customer_portal.buying_tips: Check what customers can do in each portal: view schedules and job status, pay invoices, download past invoices, approve quotes, request service, and (for custom work) make selections. Buildertrend and JobTread include client portals with selections for custom home work. Also check whether portal updates trigger text or email notifications, since customers may not visit a portal unprompted.

faqs.q: Do customers actually use customer portals?
faqs.a: We have no data on portal use. Use is easier to win when customers get a text or email that links them straight to the item (an invoice to pay, a quote to approve), so check how each portal sends those links.

faqs.q: Can customers schedule new service through the portal?
faqs.a: Some portals let customers send a service request, which the office then confirms. Self-booking into an open time slot is a separate online booking feature, so check which one a tool offers.

faqs.q: How does portal differ from a mobile app?
faqs.a: A web portal works in a phone's browser, so the customer has nothing to install. A customer app needs a download but can send push notifications. Paythepoolman, for example, sells a branded customer app (Pool Junction) as an add-on.

online_booking.name: Online Booking
online_booking.definition: Customer-facing self-scheduling with real-time technician availability.
online_booking.description: Online booking puts a scheduling form on your website where customers pick a service, choose an open time slot, enter their details and confirm, without a phone call. Fuller implementations set booking rules by service type, take a deposit at booking, send confirmations automatically, and accept bookings from ads such as Google Local Services.
online_booking.why_matters: Online booking takes requests when the office is closed. Without it, those requests wait for a callback, and a customer who reaches voicemail can book with whoever answers first. Letting the customer pick a slot on the spot removes that gap.
online_booking.buying_tips: Check: service types with buffer time between jobs, availability that respects the existing schedule, deposits at booking, booking forms by service type, booking from Google Local Services or other ads, and automatic confirmations and reminders. The list on this page shows which tools name the feature.

faqs.q: Can customers book emergency service through online booking?
faqs.a: Some platforms let you set up urgent service types that alert the on-call technician. Check whether a tool routes urgent bookings differently from scheduled ones before you offer emergency booking online.

faqs.q: How do I prevent low-quality leads from online booking?
faqs.a: Two options: take a deposit at booking (for example a service-call fee credited toward the final invoice), and ask qualifying questions for each service type before showing open times. Check that a tool supports both.

faqs.q: Does online booking work for high-ticket installation work?
faqs.a: Large jobs such as system replacements, roofs or remodels need a visit and a custom quote, so online booking for them means booking the estimate visit rather than the job. Fixed-scope work such as tune-ups and routine repairs fits self-booking better.

team_management.name: Team Management
team_management.definition: Multi-user workflows for scheduling, time tracking, communication, and compliance across technicians.
team_management.description: Team management covers the employee side of field service software: technician roles and permissions, a time clock with GPS, team chat, tracking of certifications and licenses with expiry dates, training and onboarding, and payroll integration.
team_management.why_matters: With several technicians, the business has to schedule shifts, track hours, keep certifications current and communicate without personal group chats. Without tools for that, it lives in spreadsheets and phone threads that are hard to search and easy to lose when people leave.
team_management.buying_tips: There are three approaches: a field service platform with team features built in; a field service platform plus a workforce app such as Connecteam, which runs alongside it for the time clock, scheduling, chat, training and documents; or, for very small teams, the field service tool alone. Check which of these your current tool supports before adding another subscription.

faqs.q: When do I need team management features?
faqs.a: When tracking hours, certifications and communication by hand starts costing office time or causing mistakes, such as a lapsed license or a missed shift. Compliance (certifications across states) and communication (replacing group chats) are two reasons to add it.

faqs.q: Should I use Connecteam alongside my FSM?
faqs.a: Connecteam is a workforce app for the employee side (time clock, shift scheduling, chat, training and documents) and does not do quotes, invoicing or customer portals, so it runs alongside a field service tool such as Jobber or Housecall Pro. Its pricing is per hub, with a flat monthly price covering the first 30 users and a free plan for up to 10 users.

faqs.q: How do I track technician certifications?
faqs.a: Store each certification (for example EPA Section 608 or a state license) with its expiry date and set a reminder before it lapses. Some field service platforms track this; workforce apps such as Connecteam keep certifications and licenses in document storage. Ask each vendor to show expiry reminders in a demo.

inventory.name: Inventory Management
inventory.definition: Tracking parts, materials, and equipment across vehicles and warehouses with usage automation.
inventory.description: Inventory tracking in field service software covers parts on each truck, warehouse stock, low-stock alerts, deducting parts automatically when they are added to a work order, ordering from suppliers, barcode or QR scanning for counts, and assigning part costs to jobs so job profit is accurate. It matters more in trades where parts are a large part of each job.
inventory.why_matters: Loose inventory control costs money in several ways: parts that go missing, the wrong part on the truck and a return trip, too much stock tying up cash, and part costs recorded against the wrong job, which hides which services make money.
inventory.buying_tips: Look for: stock per vehicle (not just the warehouse), automatic deduction when parts go on a work order, low-stock alerts with reorder suggestions, supplier ordering, barcode or QR scanning, and part costs assigned to jobs. Supplier ordering differs by trade; in roofing, for example, AccuLynx, JobNimbus and Roofr list ordering from ABC Supply, SRS Distribution and QXO. Some tools have no inventory at all: Jobber advertises no inventory management on any plan.

faqs.q: Do I need inventory tracking if my parts are simple?
faqs.a: We have no data on payback. If you stock few parts on few trucks, tracking may take more time than it saves; the more parts and stocked trucks you have, the more missing parts and return trips it can catch, so test it on one truck first.

faqs.q: How do I track inventory across multiple vehicles?
faqs.a: Platforms with per-vehicle inventory give each truck its own stock. When a technician uses a part on a work order, the platform deducts it from that truck and can prompt a reorder when stock runs low. Check that a tool supports stock by truck, not just a single warehouse count.

faqs.q: Should inventory integrate with my suppliers?
faqs.a: If you order often, yes: ordering from the platform saves calling the supplier or using a separate website. Check which suppliers each tool connects to; in roofing, AccuLynx, JobNimbus and Roofr list ABC Supply, SRS Distribution and QXO, and JobTread lists The Home Depot, SRS Distribution and QXO.

gps_tracking.name: GPS Tracking
gps_tracking.definition: Real-time location tracking of technician vehicles for dispatching, route verification, and accountability.
gps_tracking.description: GPS tracking serves three purposes: dispatching (sending the nearest technician to a new job), checking routes (seeing where each vehicle went), and customer ETA notifications (telling customers when their technician is on the way). It can come from the technician's phone through the field service app, with no extra hardware, or from devices installed in the vehicles.
gps_tracking.why_matters: Knowing where each technician is lets the office send the nearest one to a new job, see where time goes during the day, and send customers accurate ETAs, which cuts down on 'where is my tech' calls.
gps_tracking.buying_tips: Two options: GPS from the technician's phone through the field service app (no hardware, but it depends on the phone being on), or vehicle telematics from a fleet tracking provider such as Samsara, Geotab or Verizon Connect, which some platforms integrate with (Docket lists Samsara and Verizon Connect; Routeware lists Samsara and Geotab). Check which one each field service tool supports.

faqs.q: Can I track technicians' phones or do I need vehicle GPS?
faqs.a: Field service apps with GPS use the technician's phone, so no hardware is needed. Vehicle devices track the vehicle whether or not the technician is in it, and they are a separate subscription. Pick by whether you need to track people or vehicles.

faqs.q: What if techs turn off their phone GPS?
faqs.a: Phone-based tracking stops when location is turned off. Ask each vendor whether its app reports when location is off. A device installed in the vehicle cannot be switched off from a phone, which is one reason fleets use them.

faqs.q: How does GPS enable customer ETA notifications?
faqs.a: When a technician starts driving to a job, the platform can use the phone's location to send the customer a text with an arrival estimate. Check whether a tool sends these automatically and whether you can edit the message.

automated_marketing.name: Automated Marketing
automated_marketing.definition: Email and SMS sequences for customer retention, lead nurturing, and recurring service reminders.
automated_marketing.description: Automated marketing in field service software covers messages to customers you already have: a thank-you and review request after a job, reminders for recurring service (yearly tune-ups, quarterly treatments), seasonal campaigns, follow-ups on unsold quotes, and win-back messages. Some platforms build this in, and others connect to email tools such as Mailchimp or Constant Contact.
automated_marketing.why_matters: Maintenance reminders, seasonal offers and review requests to customers you already have only go out if someone sends them. Automation sends them on schedule instead of when someone in the office remembers.
automated_marketing.buying_tips: Test three things: recurring service reminders with a booking link, review requests sent automatically after a job, and follow-up sequences on unsold quotes. Housecall Pro, Workiz, RealGreen, FieldRoutes and PestPac name marketing automation among their features; Jobber, Housecall Pro and ServiceTitan list Mailchimp integrations. Check whether texts cost extra.

faqs.q: What's the ROI of automated marketing for trades shops?
faqs.a: We have no data on returns; they depend on your customer list, your trade and how consistently the campaigns run. Measure against your own baseline: track repeat-customer revenue and review count before and after you switch it on.

faqs.q: Can FSM marketing replace dedicated email marketing tools?
faqs.a: For service reminders, post-job thank-yous and review requests, built-in field service marketing can be enough. For newsletters and broader campaigns, dedicated email tools such as Mailchimp offer more, and several field service platforms connect to them.

faqs.q: How do I send seasonal campaigns from FSM software?
faqs.a: Check whether a tool can pick customers by service history and area (for example, everyone who had a tune-up last year but has not booked one this year) and send to that list. If it cannot, export the list or use its Mailchimp integration if it has one.

review_management.name: Review Management
review_management.definition: Automated requests for Google, Facebook, and other online reviews after job completion, with response workflows.
review_management.description: Review management automates asking for reviews. It sends a text or email request soon after the job, with links to your Google or Facebook review pages, and some tools add reply templates and a dashboard of new reviews.
review_management.why_matters: Google says more reviews and positive ratings can help a business's local ranking. Automating the request means every customer is asked right after the job, not only when someone remembers.
review_management.buying_tips: Look for: an automatic text request soon after the job is marked complete, one-click links to your review pages, and a way to reply to reviews. Check Google's current review policies before you filter who gets asked: Google prohibits businesses from discouraging negative reviews or selectively soliciting positive reviews from customers.

faqs.q: What's the typical conversion rate on automated review requests?
faqs.a: We have no data on response rates. Ask every customer soon after the job, and track how many reviews you get per request sent before and after you turn it on.

faqs.q: How does negative-review intercept work?
faqs.a: Some tools ask customers to rate the job first and send only happy customers to a public review site, routing unhappy ones to the office. Google's policy prohibits businesses from discouraging negative reviews or selectively soliciting positive reviews, so this kind of filtering can break Google's rules. Ask every customer for a review, and handle complaints separately.

faqs.q: Should I ask for reviews on Google or Facebook?
faqs.a: Google says more reviews and positive ratings can help a business's local ranking, so Google reviews matter for local search. Facebook reviews show on your Facebook page. You can link to both in one request.

membership_management.name: Membership Management
membership_management.definition: Recurring service plans with auto-renewal billing, member-priority dispatching, and tier-specific pricing.
membership_management.description: Membership or maintenance plan management runs the recurring side of a trade business: plan signup with automatic renewal billing, priority dispatch for members, pricing that differs by plan tier, renewal reminders, scheduled plan visits (such as yearly HVAC tune-ups or quarterly pest treatments), and a place for customers to manage their plan.
membership_management.why_matters: For HVAC, plumbing, pest control and pool service businesses that sell maintenance or service plans, the plans are recurring revenue. Run in spreadsheets, plans leak revenue through missed renewals, failed payments and missed visits.
membership_management.buying_tips: Check: plan tiers with different prices and benefits, automatic renewal billing with retries for failed payments, a member flag for dispatchers, plan visit schedules, and customer-facing plan management. Examples from our data: ServiceTitan lists membership management, FieldEdge includes service agreements with renewal and billing automation, Housecall Pro adds recurring service plans on MAX, FieldRoutes runs recurring services with AutoPay for pest and lawn companies, and Skimmer runs recurring pool billing with AutoPay.

faqs.q: What does a typical HVAC membership plan look like?
faqs.a: Plans differ by shop. One structure is a yearly fee for maintenance visits (for example a cooling check and a heating check) plus extras such as priority service or a repair discount. Price the plan so the visits cover their own cost.

faqs.q: How does member-priority dispatching work?
faqs.a: When a member calls, the platform shows their plan status so the dispatcher can schedule them ahead of non-members. It matters on busy days when the schedule is full. Check that a tool shows member status at the moment the call or booking comes in.

faqs.q: Can membership plans handle commercial customers?
faqs.a: Commercial agreements can cover several buildings, with their own schedules and approvals. ServiceTrade and BuildOps are built for commercial contractors and run service agreements that generate scheduled visits; check per-site pricing and schedules in a demo.

consumer_financing.name: Consumer Financing
consumer_financing.definition: In-app financing offers (such as Wisetack, GreenSky or Sunbit) for big-ticket repairs and installations.
consumer_financing.description: Consumer financing integrations let customers pay for large repairs and installations in monthly payments instead of all at once. Fuller implementations show financing options inside the quote with a short application and a quick decision, and the lender pays you. It matters for large jobs such as HVAC system replacements, roofs, panel upgrades and remodels.
consumer_financing.why_matters: Offering a monthly payment at the moment of decision gives a customer with a large bill another option besides putting the job off. Ask each financing partner for its approval terms and merchant fees before you count on it.
consumer_financing.buying_tips: The fullest implementations show the monthly payment inside the quote, so the customer can apply without leaving it. Ask each platform which lenders it supports, whether the application happens inside the quote, and who pays the lender's fee. Check lender restrictions too: Wisetack financing through Jobber requires a US business and excludes pool and spa, residential and commercial cleaning, window washing and snow removal businesses.

faqs.q: Which financing providers do FSM platforms integrate with?
faqs.a: Examples from our data: Housecall Pro, Jobber, Contractor+, PaintScout, RealGreen, SmartMoving and Floorzap offer Wisetack; ServiceTitan works with GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance; FieldEdge with GreenSky and the Optimus marketplace; AccuLynx with GreenSky; Workiz and Skimmer with Sunbit; and Service Fusion and JobTread with Acorn Finance. Check which lenders your platform supports before you choose.

faqs.q: How much do financing providers charge the contractor?
faqs.a: Financing programs can charge the contractor a merchant fee, also called a dealer fee, on each financed job, deducted from your payout, and the fee can rise for longer or promotional zero-interest terms. Ask each lender for its fee schedule before you offer it.

faqs.q: Can I offer multiple financing options?
faqs.a: Some platforms work with more than one lender; ServiceTitan, for example, lists GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance. Lenders approve different credit profiles, so a second option can help a customer the first one declines. Ask which lenders your platform supports and whether customers can compare offers in one application.

phone_system.name: Phone System (VoIP)
phone_system.definition: Native phone calling, call routing, and call recording integrated with customer records.
phone_system.description: A built-in phone system (VoIP) puts calls inside the field service platform: the caller's record pops up when the phone rings, calls are recorded and tied to the customer, missed calls route to voicemail or an after-hours queue, the office can click to call from any record, and texts run from the same number. Workiz includes a phone system, Service Fusion lists a VoIP phone system (integrated voice from its Plus plan), and Albi includes calling with call recording on its office seat.
phone_system.why_matters: Businesses that depend on inbound calls lose jobs when calls go unanswered. A built-in phone system helps three ways: the dispatcher sees customer history before answering, every call is recorded against the customer, and after-hours calls can route to the on-call tech.
phone_system.buying_tips: A built-in phone system matters more where the phone brings in the work: locksmith, emergency plumbing, garage door and appliance repair. Check call routing rules, after-hours handling, call recording, texting from the same number, and whether you can keep your existing number. If your call volume is low, a separate phone system connected to your field service tool may be enough.

faqs.q: Can I keep my existing phone number with FSM VoIP?
faqs.a: US rules on number portability let you move a phone number between providers; ask the vendor whether it supports porting your number and how long it takes. Keep the old service running until the port completes.

faqs.q: How does call recording help my business?
faqs.a: Recordings help with training (how new staff handle calls), disputes (what was agreed on the phone) and quality (common questions and objections). Ask how long each platform keeps recordings, and check your state's rules on telling callers they are recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need an AI receptionist with my phone system?
faqs.a: It is optional. An AI receptionist answers calls that would otherwise reach voicemail, such as after hours or when every line is busy; Workiz's Genius Answering, for example, answers missed calls and books jobs (by plan or add-on). Test it on real calls before you rely on it.

call_masking.name: Call Masking
call_masking.definition: Anonymized phone numbers for technician-customer communication that preserve privacy and call records.
call_masking.description: Call masking routes calls and texts between technicians and customers through a business number, so neither side sees the other's personal number. The customer sees a number tied to the business, not the technician's own phone, and the call is logged against the customer record. Workiz lists call masking among its features.
call_masking.why_matters: Masking solves two problems: privacy (technicians do not hand out personal numbers, and customers know who is calling) and record-keeping (every technician-customer conversation is captured in the platform instead of on personal phones). It also means customers keep calling the business, not the technician, if that technician leaves.
call_masking.buying_tips: Call masking matters more when technicians use their own phones to contact customers. If your team uses company phones and stays put, it matters less. Ask whether masking is included in the plan you are considering or charged separately.

faqs.q: How does call masking actually work?
faqs.a: The platform assigns a business number to the conversation. When the technician calls it, the call goes to the customer; when the customer calls back, it goes to the technician. Both see only the business number, and calls and texts are logged in the customer record.

faqs.q: Can customers still text our techs directly?
faqs.a: Through the masked number, yes, and those texts are logged. Texts to a technician's personal phone bypass the system, so masking only works if technicians do not hand out their own numbers.

faqs.q: Do I need call masking for a small shop?
faqs.a: It matters less for a small team on company phones. It matters more as you add technicians who use their own phones, or if you want customer relationships to stay with the business when someone leaves.

ai_dispatcher.name: AI Dispatcher
ai_dispatcher.definition: AI-assisted job assignment that recommends or assigns a technician for each job based on skill, location, history and availability.
ai_dispatcher.description: AI dispatch tools recommend a technician for each incoming job, or assign one automatically in some setups, by weighing factors such as location, skills and certifications, the existing schedule and past performance. ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro, for example, uses technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates, and BuildOps's OpsAI handles smart dispatch for commercial contractors.
ai_dispatcher.why_matters: On busy days, a dispatcher juggling many calls can send the wrong skill, the wrong area or a double-booked technician. Suggested assignments handle the routine choices so the dispatcher can focus on emergencies and unusual jobs.
ai_dispatcher.buying_tips: Ask what factors the tool weighs for each assignment, whether it learns from your own job history, how easily a dispatcher can override a suggestion, and whether it uses your skill and certification records. For a small team where one person sees the whole board, a suggestion engine may add little.

faqs.q: When does AI dispatching pay for itself?
faqs.a: We have no data on payback. It can help when call volume is high enough that one dispatcher cannot weigh every option for every call, such as on peak-season days. Test it on your own busiest days during a trial or pilot.

faqs.q: Can AI dispatchers replace human dispatchers entirely?
faqs.a: Treat it as help for the dispatcher. AI suggestions cover routine assignments; emergencies, unclear job descriptions that need a callback, key customers and exceptions still need a person, and the dispatcher should be able to override any suggestion.

faqs.q: Does AI dispatching work better than route optimization?
faqs.a: They solve different problems. Route optimization orders a scheduled day's stops to reduce drive time, which suits route work such as pest control, lawn care and pool service. AI dispatching assigns incoming calls to a technician in real time, which suits on-demand work. A business with both kinds of work can use both.

ai_receptionist.name: AI Receptionist (AI Phone Agent)
ai_receptionist.definition: AI-powered phone agent that answers calls, qualifies leads, and books service appointments without human intervention.
ai_receptionist.description: AI receptionists answer inbound calls when no one is available, such as after hours, on weekends or when every line is busy. The AI greets the caller, asks questions, identifies the service needed, checks availability and books an appointment. Examples from our data: Workiz's Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls in English, Spanish or French and books jobs, Jobber's Plus plan includes an AI Receptionist, Roofr sells an AI Receptionist add-on, Skimmer sells AI Phone as an add-on, and SmartMoving and Supermove describe AI agents that answer inbound calls.
ai_receptionist.why_matters: An emergency caller who reaches voicemail can call the next business on the list. An AI receptionist can answer and book those calls with no one on duty, which matters in on-demand trades such as locksmith, emergency plumbing and garage door work.
ai_receptionist.buying_tips: Test with your own call scenarios before committing: a routine booking, an emergency, a caller with a question it cannot answer, and a caller who wants a person. Check that it can transfer to a person or schedule a callback, how it is priced (per call, per minute or per plan), and how bookings appear on your schedule.

faqs.q: How do customers react to AI receptionists?
faqs.a: We have no data on caller reactions. Callers with a routine booking may be served well; callers with a complex problem may want a person. Set it up to hand complex calls to a person or a quick callback, and listen to recordings of the first weeks of calls.

faqs.q: What percentage of after-hours calls does AI capture?
faqs.a: We have no data on capture rates. Count your missed calls for a month, run the AI receptionist for a month, and compare how many of those calls became booked jobs. Ask the vendor how it is priced (per call, per minute or per plan) before you start.

faqs.q: Can AI receptionists handle emergency service routing?
faqs.a: Some can ask questions to judge urgency and send emergencies to the on-call technician instead of booking the next open slot. Test with emergency scenarios before you rely on it, and make sure emergencies reach a person.

quickbooks_integration.name: QuickBooks Integration
quickbooks_integration.definition: A sync between field service software and QuickBooks for customers, invoices, payments and accounts, one way or two way depending on the tool.
quickbooks_integration.description: A QuickBooks integration moves records between your field service tool and your books: customers, invoices created in the field service tool, payments collected there, and the mapping of line items to income accounts. Integrations differ on two points: which edition they support (QuickBooks Online, Desktop or both) and which way the sync runs. Jobber syncs one way to QuickBooks Online only, Housecall Pro syncs with QuickBooks Online and one way to QuickBooks Desktop (QuickBooks sync starts on its Essentials plan), Knowify syncs both ways with QuickBooks Online and with Desktop on its Enterprise plan, and FieldEdge markets a real-time, two-way integration.
quickbooks_integration.why_matters: Without an integration, office staff retype invoices and payments from the field service tool into QuickBooks, and the work grows with job volume. A two-way sync also avoids the two systems showing different customer balances, which causes collection mistakes.
quickbooks_integration.buying_tips: Verify three things before committing: which QuickBooks edition the tool supports (Online, Desktop or both); which way the sync runs (a one-way push from the field service tool, or two way); and whether you can map line items to your own income accounts. Some tools export a file instead of syncing: RealGreen exports a general ledger file for QuickBooks, and PestPac exports financial totals.

faqs.q: Does my FSM platform support QuickBooks Desktop?
faqs.a: It varies. Jobber syncs with QuickBooks Online only. Housecall Pro syncs one way to QuickBooks Desktop. Service Fusion, FieldPulse and JobNimbus support Desktop as well as Online, Knowify offers Desktop sync on its Enterprise plan, and FieldEdge is built around QuickBooks. If your accountant uses Desktop, test the sync before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sync historical data when I switch FSM platforms?
faqs.a: Ask before you switch: some integrations sync only new records from the day you connect them, and older history stays in the old system or in QuickBooks. Ask the new vendor what it can import and from when, and keep access to your old system's exports.

faqs.q: What happens when QuickBooks and FSM disagree on a customer balance?
faqs.a: Ask each vendor which system wins when records conflict (for example customer details in the field service tool and payment status in QuickBooks), and how duplicate customers are handled. Test with a real customer who exists in both systems before you go live.

two_way_texting.name: Two-Way SMS Texting
two_way_texting.definition: Send and receive text messages with customers from within the FSM platform, with conversation history tied to customer records.
two_way_texting.description: Two-way texting puts text conversations inside the field service platform, so every message to or from a customer is saved on their record. Fuller implementations text from a business number (not a technician's personal phone), support photos, send automatic appointment reminders and ETA messages, and let the office text from any customer record. Jobber, JobNimbus, Floorzap and Network Leads list two-way texting; on Service Autopilot it is an upper-tier item priced on request.
two_way_texting.why_matters: Customers text to confirm appointments, ask quick questions and send photos of a problem. Without two-way texting in the platform, those texts land on personal phones and are lost when a technician leaves. Keeping them on the customer record gives the whole office the history.
two_way_texting.buying_tips: Look for: texting from a business number through the platform, photo messages, automatic templates (appointment reminders, ETA notices, post-job thanks), and texting from any customer or job record. Check whether texts cost extra: some platforms charge for messages or sell message packs.

faqs.q: Why is two-way texting better than email for customer communication?
faqs.a: For quick, time-sensitive messages (appointment confirmations, ETA updates, short questions), a text is easy to read and answer on a phone. Email still suits invoices and longer documents.

faqs.q: Are there compliance requirements for business SMS?
faqs.a: Yes. Texting customers is regulated (the Telephone Consumer Protection Act in the US, and Canada's anti-spam law, CASL), and marketing texts in particular need the customer's consent and a way to opt out. Ask the platform how it records consent and handles opt-out replies, and get legal advice for your situation.

faqs.q: Can I send mass marketing SMS to my customer list?
faqs.a: Send marketing texts only to customers who have agreed to receive them, and give them a way to opt out. Check how each platform records consent and handles opt-outs, whether it supports broadcast messages, and what each message costs.
